units.text: Begin with the clock hardware on the left. Precision-time placement groups place supported instances on infrastructure with access to high-precision time sources. Confirm support for the intended instance and location.

Move to the configuration checklist. Enhanced Amazon Time Sync capabilities depend on the supported operating system and configuration. Validate the actual synchronization method instead of assuming placement alone configures the guest clock.

Compare the three requirements in the next panel. Clock accuracy, network locality and failure isolation are distinct. Where supported, a cluster group can specify a precision-time parent, but each capability still needs its own design checks.

With the whole slide restored, follow the measurement panel on the right. Verify clock behavior against the application's needs, and separately provide replication, backups and Availability Zone resilience.

Start at CPU and credits. CPU utilization measures processor use; burstable instances also expose credit balances and consumption. For Unlimited mode, inspect surplus-credit behavior when assessing sustained demand and cost.

Move to the network panel. Network input and output measure bytes, while packet metrics expose a different dimension of demand. Compare the measured traffic with the selected instance's bandwidth and packet-rate limits.

Inspect local disk versus EBS. The disk operation and disk byte metrics shown here describe instance-store activity. For EBS, select the appropriate volume metrics and supported instance-level EBS metrics.

Look inside the guest. Memory utilization and filesystem free space require configured guest collection, such as the CloudWatch agent, or custom metrics. Their absence from standard EC2 metrics does not mean those resources are healthy.

Read the resolution panel below. Basic monitoring is generally five minutes, while detailed monitoring provides eligible metrics every minute. Check each metric's own reporting cadence and choose a statistic and period appropriate to the question.

With the full slide visible, trace every signal back to its source. High CPU, storage pressure and low available memory require different evidence. Diagnose the bottleneck before resizing or changing the architecture.
